checks.message: Shield Advanced is $3,000/month with a 1-year commitment — verify this is intentional
checks.context: Evaluate your actual DDoS risk profile before subscribing. For most workloads, Shield Standard (free) plus WAF is sufficient. Shield Advanced makes sense for high-profile public-facing services.

checks.message: Associate a Route 53 health check for health-based detection
checks.context: Without a health check, Shield Advanced can't distinguish a DDoS attack from a legitimate traffic spike. A health check enables proactive engagement with the AWS DDoS Response Team.

checks.message: Enable all data sources — S3 protection, EKS audit logs, and malware protection are off by default
checks.context: A detector with only CloudTrail and VPC flow logs misses S3 data events, Kubernetes API activity, and malware on EC2. Enable all data sources for complete coverage.

checks.message: Deleting a GuardDuty detector removes all threat detection for this region
checks.context: All findings, suppression rules, and threat intelligence are destroyed. Disabling GuardDuty is one of the first things attackers do after gaining access. Verify this is intentional.

checks.message: Disassociating removes this account's findings from the central security console
checks.context: Your security team's GuardDuty administrator account will no longer see findings from this account. Threats in this account become invisible to centralized monitoring.

checks.message: Use DNS validation — email validation is fragile and doesn't auto-renew
checks.context: Email validation sends to WHOIS contacts that are often wrong or outdated. DNS validation is automated, doesn't expire, and auto-renews without manual intervention.

checks.message: Verify the certificate is not in use before deleting
checks.context: Deleting a certificate still associated with a CloudFront distribution, ALB, or API Gateway causes HTTPS to fail immediately. ACM warns you if it's in use, but verify manually.

checks.message: The private key must never be stored in git, S3 without encryption, or shared via chat
checks.context: Importing a certificate requires the private key on the command line. That key must be stored in Secrets Manager or KMS-encrypted storage — not in your shell history or a text file.

checks.message: Validation emails are sent to WHOIS contacts — verify the domain owner will receive them
checks.context: If the WHOIS contacts are outdated or incorrect, the validation email will go to the wrong person. Consider switching to DNS validation for automated, reliable certificate issuance.

checks.message: Malware scan creates a snapshot of the EBS volume — verify the instance is in a supported region
checks.context: GuardDuty malware protection creates an EBS snapshot for scanning. This incurs snapshot storage costs. Scans can take minutes to hours depending on volume size.
